description: An app development company for New York businesses: iOS, Android and web apps, MVPs, payments and app store launch, scoped in writing and supported after.
h1: An app development company for New York businesses with a real product to ship
intro: 22 Signals is an app development company New York businesses use to build iOS and Android apps, web apps and SaaS products. We scope the first version tightly, design it with your users, build payments and APIs, take it through App Store and Google Play review, and support it after launch, with one Signal Lead answering for the whole thing.

sections.h: Why New York app projects run over
p: The usual story goes like this. A company in Midtown or the Flatiron District decides it needs an app: a client app for a wealth manager, a resident app for a building portfolio, a booking app for a group of clinics. A studio quotes a number, the scope grows in every meeting, the release date slips twice, and the first version ships with features nobody uses while the one thing customers asked for is still on the list.

Most of that is avoidable. The fix is deciding what version one must do, writing it down, and saying no to the rest until real users have tried it. Any app development company New York teams hire should push back on scope, not just accept it. In practice the first version usually ends up much smaller than the original wish list, and the cut features wait in a written backlog with a reason next to each one.

Real estate: resident apps for rent payment, maintenance requests, amenity booking and package alerts

p: An app holds more personal data than most websites: names, locations, payment details, sometimes health or financial records. The SHIELD Act asks any business holding private information about New York residents to keep reasonable safeguards, and the state's breach law sets a 30-day deadline to notify affected residents. So we encrypt data in transit and at rest, keep secrets off the device, log access, and collect only what the feature needs.

Apple and Google both review apps before release and reject them for privacy labels that do not match the code, payment flows that bypass in-app purchase rules, or missing account deletion. We plan for those rules at the design stage so review is a formality, not a setback.

sections.h: Proof: over $1.5 million in projects managed
p: We have managed over $1.5 million in projects, and the lesson that carries across all of them is simple: the budget holds when the scope is written down and every change is priced before it is built. On app work that means a signed list of screens and features for version one, a backlog for everything else, and a demo of working software every two weeks so you never wait months to see progress.

sections.h: How sprints, demos and bug fixes run
p: Each sprint ends with a demo and a written list of what shipped, what moved and what is next. Demos are booked at times that suit your team, and bugs your testers report go into one shared board with a priority and a fix date. App work is remote by nature: test builds arrive through TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, and designs live in shared files.
For user research with customers in the city or a launch workshop, we come to New York when the project needs it.

p: An app is only useful if people download it and keep using it. Many app studios stop at the store launch. Because we also run paid media, SEO, video and 3D, the same team that builds your app can make the store screenshots and preview video, run the install campaigns and build the landing page. If the app needs AI features, our custom AI development team builds them in. Related: web development, custom AI development, cloud consulting and paid media.

faqs.q: Should we build a native app or a cross-platform app?
faqs.a: Cross-platform frameworks like React Native or Flutter suit most business apps and cost less to maintain, because one codebase serves iOS and Android. Native makes sense when you need heavy device features, top performance or very platform-specific design. We recommend after seeing your feature list, not before.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build an app?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. A focused MVP is far quicker than a full product with payments, roles and integrations. We give you dates in writing after the planning stage, once screens and features are agreed, and show working software every two weeks so you can see progress against them.

faqs.q: Do you build fintech or crypto apps for New York companies?
faqs.a: We build fintech front ends, onboarding and dashboards, and we design with New York rules in mind. Virtual currency businesses serving New York need an NYDFS license, and licensed firms must meet Part 500 cybersecurity controls. Licensing is your legal team's job; we make sure the app supports the controls they commit to.

Ownership of the source code, app store accounts, cloud accounts and designs is agreed in writing at the start, and you always have access to what we build and run for you, so there is no lock-in if you later move the work in-house.

faqs.q: Can we meet the team in New York?
faqs.a: Most of the work runs remotely, with demos and reviews booked at times that suit you. If user interviews with your New York customers or a launch workshop would help, we can come to the city when the project needs it, agreed in writing during planning.

faqs.q: What does app development cost for a New York company?
faqs.a: Cost depends on platforms, number of screens and roles, integrations, compliance and support. We do not publish prices because those factors swing the total widely. After a 15-minute call and a short scoping session, we send a written estimate tied to a written feature list.
